India’s Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) calculates it using eight pollutants, including PM2.5, PM10, nitrogen dioxide, sulphur dioxide and carbon monoxide.

points: Girls' Education: More than 2.6 million Afghan girls remain barred from secondary school, while women continue to be excluded from universities, according to a new United Nations report on Afghanistan's education crisis.

Speaking during an X Spaces session hosted by #Finance Daily on Thursday, Alhajji said Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Kuwait, and Iraq are pursuing measures ranging from new pipeline routes to storage facilities in overseas markets, potentially reshaping regional…

According to OPEC estimates, in 2026, freight rates for a VLCC carrying crude from the Middle East to East Asia has risen about 12 times, from $3.18/barrel at the end of January 2026 to $37.13/barrel at the end of October 2026.

He noted that costs of approximately $40/barrel is manageable when crude is at $115–120/barrel, but at $70 producers would be left with about $30 per barrel, potentially inducing investment cuts, and triggering another crisis loop in the industry.

items.title: DOF wins more AHTS work offshore Canada
points: Norwegian offshore vessel owner DOF has secured a contract extension for its anchor handling tug supply (AHTS) vessel Skandi Mariner, which is working offshore Canada.
The company said an option under the vessel’s existing charter had been exercised, extending its firm employment from the second quarter of 2027 until the third quarter of 2028.

The extension is valued between $15m and $25m While DOF did not identify the customer in its latest announcement, its earlier investor presentations state that the vessel has been working for Canadian energy company Cenovus Energy.
The 2017-built Skandi Mariner secured an initial two-year contract with Cenovus, commencing in the second quarter of 2025, to support the development of the White Rose field offshore Newfoundland.
The 95-metre vessel entered the Canadian market alongside the Skandi Mover, which secured a separate 5.5-year agreement with the same operator.
Both vessels were involved in the tow-out of the West White Rose concrete gravity structure during 2025.

points: Thiruvananthapuram, TDB president K Jayakumar on Monday said there were concerns over a possible shortage of ghee at Sabarimala and steps were being taken to procure additional stocks.

items.title: Mumbai Bans Rockets, Aerial Crackers Till November 25 After Diwali Fires
points: In the wake of multiple fire incidents across the city, the Mumbai Disaster Management Authority on Monday banned the bursting of rockets and aerial firecrackers in the metropolis until November 25.
According to the order issued by the authority, the restriction covers all residential buildings, rooftops, balconies, and slum pockets.
Three major fires were reported in different parts of the city on Diwali night alone, gutting several huts, shops, a garage, and parts of a commercial building.

The order, signed by additional municipal commissioner Prajakta Verma-Lavangare, cited the risk posed by rockets and other firecrackers that fly into the sky and land on rooftops, balconies, windows and other combustible materials, potentially triggering…

items.title: A.E. Nomikos adds Oshima kamsarmax to fleet renewal drive
points: Nomikos Shipping Investments has returned to Japan’s Oshima Shipbuilding for a kamsarmax newbuilding, continuing its fleet renewal programme with a vessel scheduled to join its fleet towards the end of the decade.
The Piraeus-based company confirmed the contract was signed with Sumisho Marine involved in the deal.
Shipbroking sources have placed delivery in 2029, although the owner’s website lists the vessel for 2030.
The 82,000 dwt newbuilding, provisionally named Leontari SB, has already been added to the company’s fleet register.
Nomikos said the order marked another step in its efforts to renew and expand its fleet, maintaining its long-standing focus on Japanese-built tonnage.
Established in 1985, the Greek company currently operates four bulk carriers, including the 2009-built, 82,553 dwt Astraea SB, also constructed at Oshima.
Its remaining fleet comprises three smaller bulkers built by Japan Marine United between 2014 and 2015: the 60,990 dwt sisterships Filosofia SB and Attiki SB, and the 55,685 dwt Alkyoni SB.

items.title: Winter is coming! Voltas delivers strong Q2 results. Should you buy the Tata Group AC maker as cold winds rise?
points: Voltas share price rose 2.5% on Monday, 9 November, after the Tata Group company reported a strong performance for the September quarter of FY27.

Air conditioning and cooling solutions maker Voltas Ltd posted a 51.4% year-on-year (YoY) increase in consolidated net profit to ₹47.71 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with ₹31.5 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Revenue from operations grew 15.3% YoY to ₹2,706.57 crore in the September quarter, against ₹2,347.32 crore a year earlier, according to the company's regulatory filing.
Revenue from Voltas' Unitary Cooling Products segment, which includes its room air conditioner business, increased 29% to ₹1,566.79 crore in Q2 FY27 from ₹1,215.13 crore in the year-ago quarter.
Revenue from the Electro-Mechanical Projects and Services segment declined 15.5% YoY to ₹816.39 crore in Q2 FY27.
Meanwhile, revenue from the Engineering Products and Services segment increased 33.32% to ₹185.39 crore, supported by growth in Mining and Construction Equipment and Textile Machinery.

items.title: A2B-online turns to China for methanol-ready boxship pair
points: Dutch shortsea container operator A2B-online has ordered two more methanol-capable vessels at China Merchants Industry Weihai Shipyard, doubling its fleet renewal programme to four ships.
The latest contract marks a switch to China after the company booked its first two newbuildings at Turkey’s Sedef Shipyard in 2023.
The Chinese pair will feature multi-fuel methanol propulsion, shore power connections and battery systems, allowing emission-free operations in ports and inland waterways.

A2B-online said the newbuildings will follow the same design approach developed with Hamburg-based engineering firm Technolog Services, offering double the cargo intake of its older tonnage without a significant increase in vessel length.
The vessels will eventually be deployed on the company’s shortsea network linking Moerdijk in the Netherlands with Tilbury, Immingham and Teesport in the UK.
The latest investment follows the carrier’s 2023 order for two 650 teu methanol-capable containerships at Sedef.
Those vessels, A2B Vision and A2B Progress, have been launched and are preparing to enter service.

items.title: Tende Energy hires rig for drilling work offshore Tunisia
points: Offshore drilling contractor Ocean Oilfield has secured a contract from Tende Energy to deploy its Ocean MVM jackup rig for a drilling campaign offshore Tunisia.
The rig will be used for the Abiod well programme on the Maâmoura concession in the Gulf of Hammamet, targeting a previously undeveloped fractured carbonate reservoir.
The Ocean MVM jackup was previously named Noble Resolve and was sold by Noble Corporation to Ocean Oilfield for $64m in cash in December 2025.
The planned work involves drilling a deviated sidetrack from the existing Maâmoura E2 well to bring additional hydrocarbons into production through infrastructure already in place.

According to technical information published by Anglo Tunisian Oil & Gas, the proposed Abiod well could deliver gross production exceeding 6,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, subject to successful drilling and reservoir performance.
The reservoir was discovered in 1987 and subsequently appraised in 1988, when testing demonstrated oil and gas flows.

The row stems from Kharge’s remarks when he extended his Diwali greetings to people on Saturday, saying this is a major festival celebrated by everyone across the country as it is a “khushiyon ka Eid” that lasts for a long time.

Why is it that when it comes to Diwali which has its own sanctity, tradition and identity, you choose to call it Eid while extending greetings to Hindus?” said BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia on Monday, alleging that the Congress sought to dilute…

items.title: 25-yr-old killed, friend injured in fight between two groups at Noida park: Cop
points: A 25-year-old man died, and his friend was injured after a fight broke out between two groups of men at a park near Naya Bans village in Noida’s Phase 1 area on the intervening night of Sunday and Monday, police said.
The deceased, identified as Amit, was at the park near his home with his friends Shivam, Yashpal, Akash and Vinod.
All five were residents of Naya Bans village and in their 20s.
“The incident took place around 2am when the group was leaving the park on a scooter.
This led to an argument between the two groups, which soon escalated into a fight,” said Abhay Kumar Mishra, additional deputy commissioner of police (Noida).
Police said the two groups knew each other and there was no prior enmity between them.
Both groups were residents of Naya Bans village.
“Following a complaint by Amit’s family, we registered a case under section 103 (murder) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS),” ADCP Mishra said.

items.title: SC directs Uttar Pradesh to identify undertrial prisoners languishing in jails despite getting bail
points: The Supreme Court has directed the Uttar Pradesh government to identify undertrial prisoners languishing in jails despite getting bail, saying the onus is on the state to ensure they are released.
A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale on November 4 asked the state to identify such prisoners in consultation with the District Legal Service Authorities (DLSA).

The court took up a suo motu petition on bail reforms while monitoring the implementation of its January 31, 2023, judgment directing all states and Union territories to establish a permanent mechanism to ensure the speedy release of undertrial prisoners…

The Uttar Pradesh government responded to the application and confirmed that 264 undertrial prisoners across 20 district jails had obtained bail as of September 29, 2026.
